docs.abstract: The dataset contains measurements made from three autonomous Seasonal Ice Mass Balance (SIMB) buoys. The buoys were deployed in the late summer of 2023 as part of the Alfred Wegener Institute ArcWatch Project.
docs.title: Measurements of ice mass balance and temperature from autonomous Seasonal Ice Mass Balance (SIMB3) buoys deployed in the Central Arctic Ocean on the ArcWatch expedition in 2023
contactOrganization: Thayer School of Engineering at Dartmouth College
USACE-CRREL; Thayer School of Engineering at Dartmouth College

docs.abstract: The Comprehensive Ocean - Atmosphere Data Set (COADS) Long Marine Reports Fixed-Length (LMRF) Arctic subset contains marine surface weather reports for regions north of 65 degrees N from ships, drifting ice stations, and buoys.
docs.title: Comprehensive Ocean - Atmosphere Data Set (COADS) LMRF Arctic Subset, 1950 - 1995, Version 1
origin: National Snow and Ice Data Center

docs.abstract: Fiber-optic equipped moorings for Raman backscatter Distributed Temperature Sensing (DTS) were installed at Windless Bight, Antarctica in November 2011. Continuous-in-space measurements of temperature were recorded every meter along the mooring.
docs.title: Fiber-Optic Distributed Temperature Sensing at Windless Bight, Version 1
origin: National Snow and Ice Data Center

docs.abstract: This data set contains water depth, temperature, specific gravity, salinity, and density measurements from the North Polar Basin and the Barents Sea, gathered by Nansen and crew on the Norwegian North Polar Expedition from 1893-1896.
docs.title: Norwegian North Polar Expedition 1893-1896: Oceanographic Data, Version 1
origin: National Snow and Ice Data Center

docs.abstract: This project focused on the pelagic microbes from the Kongsfjorden-Krossfjorden system located on the West coast of Spitsbergen. The West coast of Spitsbergen is influenced by the West Spitsbergen Current (WSC), which is transformed Atlantic water, characterized by relatively warm and saline water.
docs.title: Glacial melting and coastal marine microbes of the Arctic
